title: NRI Property Sale in India: Understanding Different TDS Rules
description: When a Non-Resident Indian (NRI) sells property in India, the buyer must deduct Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) at specific rates. These TDS rates for NRIs are s.

faq.q: What is the primary difference in TDS for resident vs. NRI sellers?
faq.a: For resident sellers, TDS is typically 1% on property value above ₹50 lakhs. For NRI sellers, TDS is linked to capital gains tax rates (e.g., 20% for LTCG, 30% for STCG) and is deducted on the *entire* sale consideration.

faq.q: Can an NRI seller avoid high TDS deduction?
faq.a: Yes, an NRI seller can apply for a Lower TDS Certificate under Section 197 from the Income Tax Department. This allows the buyer to deduct TDS at a rate closer to the NRI's actual tax liability.

faq.q: What are Forms 15CA and 15CB used for?
faq.a: Form 15CB is a certificate from a Chartered Accountant verifying the tax compliance of a remittance to an NRI. Form 15CA is a declaration filed online with the Income Tax Department by the remitter, based on Form 15CB, before transferring funds out of India.

faq.q: Is there a limit on how much an NRI can repatriate from property sale proceeds?
faq.a: Generally, NRIs can repatriate up to USD 1 million per financial year from NRO account funds, subject to tax compliance. However, if the property was originally purchased with NRE/FCNR(B) funds, the entire sale proceeds can be repatriated without this limit.

faq.q: What if the NRI seller has no capital gains?
faq.a: Even if there are no capital gains or a capital loss, the buyer is still obligated to deduct TDS on the gross sale consideration at the prescribed rates. The NRI seller would then need to claim a refund by filing their income tax return, or apply for a nil TDS certificate under Section 197.

faq.q: Does Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA) apply to property sales?
faq.a: Yes, DTAA provisions between India and the NRI's country of residence can be considered. A CA certifying Form 15CB will take DTAA into account, potentially offering tax relief, though the TDS will still be deducted in India as per Indian tax laws.

fact_check.summary: The article provides a largely accurate overview of NRI property sale TDS rules in India, with correct references to relevant sections of the Income Tax Act and general procedures. However, there are some inaccuracies regarding the LTCG tax rate for NRIs and the application of indexation post-July 23, 2024, as well as a minor discrepancy in the example calculation.

corrections.note: Updated the LTCG tax rate and TDS calculations for NRIs to reflect the changes effective July 23, 2024, and corrected the Cost Inflation Index for FY 2026-27.

edits.why: The claim was outdated. For properties transferred on or after July 23, 2024, LTCG for NRIs is taxed at 12.5% without indexation. The TDS rate is also aligned with this new tax rate. For transfers before this date, the 20% with indexation rule applied.
The Cost Inflation Index for FY 2026-27 has been officially notified by the CBDT as 384.
The TDS and actual tax liability calculations were updated to reflect the 12.5% LTCG tax rate for NRIs for sales on or after July 23, 2024.
